props.title: Challenge of the Tiger

sections.content: **Challenge of the Tiger** (1980) represents a fascinating intersection of exploitation cinema and martial arts, starring Bruce Le (one of many Bruce Lee imitators) alongside Richard Harrison. This Italian-Hong Kong co-production exemplifies the "Bruceploitation" phenomenon that emerged after Bruce Lee's death in 1973. Like **Game of Death** (1978) and **Fist of Fury** (1972), it capitalizes on the martial arts craze, but adds elements of spy thriller and gratuitous nudity typical of European B-movies of the era. sections.content: The exploitation cinema boom of the 1970s and 1980s birthed countless martial arts knockoffs. **The Dragon Lives Again** (1977) bizarrely featured Bruce Lee in the afterlife fighting Dracula and James Bond, while **Exit the Dragon, Enter the Tiger** (1976) starred Bruce Li in a meta-narrative about avenging Bruce Lee's death. These films, despite their obvious cash-grab nature, created their own peculiar subgenre mixing martial arts with increasingly outlandish plots.

Harrison's presence in **Challenge of the Tiger** connects to the broader phenomenon of Western actors appearing in Asian action films, similar to **The Way of the Dragon** (1972) featuring Chuck Norris. This cross-cultural pollination defined much of 1970s martial arts cinema, leading to hybrid productions like **Kill Bill: Vol. 1** (2003), which would later pay homage to this era. sections.content: The Bruceploitation movement spawned dozens of imitators with similar names: Bruce Li, Bruce Le, Bruce Lai, and Dragon Lee. Films like **The Clones of Bruce Lee** (1980) didn't even try to hide their derivative nature, instead leaning into the absurdity. This phenomenon influenced later martial arts cinema, including self-aware homages like **Kentucky Fried Movie** (1977) and **Black Dynamite** (2009).
